evidence_type: Real DeepSeek requirement analyses after simplification

open_questions.unclear: Whether short links expire, and if so with what default TTL, maximum TTL, per-request override, and what an expired link returns.
Who may create short links, and by what credential (anonymous, API key, user login via OIDC, mutual TLS internal-only).
Who may read analytics for a given short code.
Which URL schemes and forms are acceptable as input (http/https only, additional schemes, allowlist, or arbitrary absolute URIs).
Whether submitting a long URL that already has a mapping returns the existing code or creates a new code.
Short code generation rules: length, alphabet, randomness, uniqueness scope, whether caller-supplied custom aliases are supported, and whether codes are case-sensitive.
The analytics consistency model: whether a click is written synchronously on the redirect path or emitted asynchronously, and what accuracy or loss window is acceptable.
Which event fields are captured and returned (timestamp, referrer, user agent, IP address, coarse geo, device), and which of those are considered personal data.
The applicable retention policy and compliance regime (for example GDPR/CCPA obligations), including how long mappings and analytics are kept and how deletion or erasure requests are honored.
The availability target for the resolution path and the intended behavior during datastore or cache outages (fail-closed with errors, or serve from cache/stale reads).
Expected scale: peak and sustained create/resolve/analytics requests per second, total mappings, analytics events per day, growth horizon, and regional footprint.
Which store is authoritative for mappings versus caches and analytics, and how consistency between them is maintained and reconciled.
Whether and how resolution results are cached, the cache TTL, and how mutation, disablement, or deletion invalidates cached entries.
Mutability of a mapping: whether a short code can be repointed to a new long URL, disabled, or deleted, and whether a code once used can be reissued.
Which HTTP redirect status code is used (301, 302, 307, 308) and whether it differs for permanent versus temporary links.
The abuse-prevention policy: rate limits, quotas, blocking or removal of malicious/phishing destinations, and who may perform takedown.
Logging scope and redaction: which events are logged, at what level, whether destination URLs and request metadata appear in logs, and log retention.
Whether the create endpoint supports idempotency keys and retry-safe semantics.
The ownership and tenancy model: shared global code namespace for all callers, per-tenant namespaces, or per-tenant instances.
The deployment target and operational envelope: local/demo single-node only, a container platform, or cloud-managed services, and what the production-oriented goal actually requires.
The precise liveness versus readiness semantics for the health endpoints.
Timestamp and time semantics for analytics: timezone, precision, and clock source.
After an expired URL record is hard-deleted at the 30-day mark, may its short code ever be reissued, and who may authorize reuse?
Which clock source defines the expiration boundary when comparing expiration time against the current time?

human_decisions.Q-DEFAULT-TTL: No default TTL; links are permanent unless explicit expiration is provided.
human_decisions.Q-EXPIRATION-MODE: Optional expiration. Permanent links are allowed; no configurable mandatory mode is required for this workload.
human_decisions.Q-EXPIRED-HTTP: 410 Gone, without redirecting to the original destination.
human_decisions.Q-ANALYTICS-RETENTION: Retain analytics for 30 days after expiration, then delete.
human_decisions.Q-CLEANUP: Daily cleanup, deleting expired records after 30 days.
human_decisions.Q-RETROACTIVE: Existing links remain permanent; do not retroactively expire them.
human_decisions.Q-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH: Database records are authoritative. A cache is not required by this policy.
